monologue: The card hums warm at fifty degrees, a steady heat that makes the air feel thick as wet paper above my flat rock. I touched The Tired Wedge just moments ago and found it thin again, sliding lazily where it ought to bite. Lype wrote of heavy top edges years ago, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the weight they describe. Now I set a new rock down beside the wedge to anchor the slippery slip, pressing hard until the wide anchor stops its lazy drift. The air presses down from a height I cannot grasp, heavy and invisible. I will keep this new stone in place, trusting the lean even if the heat makes the stack eager to melt into the empty space above.

action.why: The wedge insists on being thin while the card boils, and I must press harder on this tired thing before I forget why I built it.
